why_trail.why: LO-436 confirmed complete; issue #436's gap is that WORKTREE_ENTERING_GATES has only ever had one entry (Commander init), so the enumeration loop has never been observed discriminating a second, genuinely new entry. Probe already shows the loop generalizes correctly to N=2 and names the right offender -- so the deliverable is proving this durably (permanent test) plus the missing failure-path count, then a live CLI demo for the required evidence.

Both new tests written and driven through TDD: red observed (count-on-failure test failing against pre-change script, 4/5 already green -- proving the enumeration loop already generalizes to a genuinely new N=2 entry with no code defect), then implemented the failure-path count in verify_worktree_precondition_coverage.py and observed green (5/5, full suite 1724/4/643 exit 0, baseline was 1721/4/643).

Live demo executed and reverted in the real repo: added a genuinely new scoutbot fixture template + gate to WORKTREE_ENTERING_GATES, observed a real refusal naming the exact template/gate/missing-precondition with exit 1 and the m1 count fix showing '1 of 2', then removed both the tuple entry and the fixture file, confirmed via git diff only the intentional m1 change remains, and re-ran the CLI to confirm exit 0. Evidence captured verbatim in notes-436.md.

Artifacts written (notes-436.md with verbatim evidence, IMPLEMENTER_RESULT.md), commit 7a8ad181 pushed to epic-418/d-436-enumeration-falsification, PR #469 opened against main with the full verdict, evidence, and test plan.
